messages:
sophia: FYI - Sienna (customer) opened a ticket: p99 latency ~2x and request queueing for model-r2 in us-west-2 since ~02:10 UTC. They see timeouts and client retries. ticket: https://support.redwood/s/CASE-12345 :exclamation:

mike: ack. any sample traces or span ids from them?

sophia: pasted a small trace in the ticket. sample req id: r2-req-4b7c. stack shows long kernel wait. logs: `2026-03-15T02:12:44Z svc:inference token_gen=195ms kernel_wait=710ms kv_hit=false`

ani: pinging infra to check GPU metrics for us-west-2 node pool used by dedicated -> will run quick perf test. can someone confirm model variant (quant vs fp16)?

david: Sienna is on variant `r2-4q` (4-bit quant) with pin to v3. They recently bumped concurrency from 32->48 yesterday.

mike: interesting. concurrency bump + quant could increase kernel contention. can we get current queue depth and allocator stats?

sophia: support-bot: attached a heap of logs and a flame snapshot uploaded: /internal/sienna/r2/2140004321/flame.svg

support-bot: Automated alert: Sienna p99 latency breached SLO at 02:09 UTC, incidents created: INC-8712. Notifying eng-runtime.

ani: running a microbenchmark now: `./bench --model r2-4q --seq 1024 --concurrency 48 --requests 500` will post numbers in ~5m.

mike: while that's running, can someone grab KV cache hit rate and kernel selector outputs? command: `redwood-metrics query --m=node_pool.us-west-2.kernel_selector`

david: KV cache hit rate dropped to 27% for that customer pattern (was ~62% previously). looks like input distribution changed (more long prompts).

julia: noted. long prompts -> bigger KV growth -> more memory pressure -> cache evictions -> more kernel recompute. could explain kernel_wait spikes.

ani: bench results: avg p50=62ms, p95=410ms, p99=890ms under concurrency 48. When I drop concurrency to 24: p99=420ms. CPU on host (pilot job) shows kernels waiting on cuda memcpy and scheduler queue.

mike: can you run same bench with `--prefill-cache` (send repeated prefixes) to see delta?

ani: ran with prefill: p99 -> 240ms. so big delta. KV cache miss rate is main lever here.

sophia: customer reported they have a new feature that concatenates long prefaces to inputs. we're likely hitting eviction/regeneration churn.

david: short-term mitigation options: 1) reduce allowed concurrency for that customer on dedicated pool, 2) bump cache size on their allocation, 3) route to r2-fp16 variant when latency critical.

mike: agree. propose we 1) apply a soft concurrency cap to their tenant to allo wheadroom, 2) schedule a midnight maintenance to increase kv cache allocation (requires restart), 3) add automatic route fallback to fp16 when p99 exceeds threshold.

julia: I can draft the rollout steps for cache bump (impact, rollback). needs ~8-10 min downtime for restart of worker group if we change allocator settings.

support-bot: Action logged: assign INC-8712 -> eng-runtime (owner: mike).

mike: I’ll own the immediate cap. setting tenant concurrency to 24 now.

(1 minute later)
mike: applied soft cap for tenancy `sienna-prod` to 24. monitoring.

(10 minutes later)
ani: after cap: observed p99 dropped to ~380ms on our bench and customer reports initial improvement (support ticket update). KV miss rate stabilized at ~45%.

sophia: customer confirmed fewer timeouts, they'll keep us posted.

david: follow-up: I'll schedule cache bump for their dedicated pool in the 03:00 UTC maintenance window. julia can you review maintenance notes?

julia: reviewing now. will post runbook steps in the ticket and add rollback: revert kv_size to previous and restart workers.

mike: next steps assign: mike -> monitor for 2h, ani -> run cross-region perf test and submit perf artifacts, david/julia -> plan cache roll, support -> update customer. Meet async here for updates. :thumbsup:
